title: Algorithm
definition: An algorithm is a finite and unambiguous procedure that transforms valid inputs into specified outputs and terminates under its stated conditions.
purpose: Establish the solution-procedure concept required before problem definition and pseudocode work.
history: Algorithms predate electronic computers; modern computing represents and executes them through formal and programmable systems.
mental_model: An algorithm is a bounded route from valid input to specified output with explicit progress and a stopping condition.
analogy: A route plan has ordered steps and a destination, but real travel may rely on human judgment not permitted in an unambiguous algorithm.
common_mistakes: Calling any task list an algorithm
industry_notes: Algorithms provide the behavior model later implemented, tested, analyzed, and maintained.
ai_notes: AI-generated algorithms require independent checks for validity, termination, correctness, and hidden assumptions.
interview_notes: Ask the candidate to explain what makes a procedure finite and unambiguous.
exercise_candidates: Identify missing input, output, or termination conditions
lab_candidates: Convert a precise daily process into a finite procedure
project_candidates: Design the algorithm contract for a simulator
